quotes.text: Enable your customers to adjust the quantity of items during checkout.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: If you use the Payment Intents API, you must manually track line item updates and modify the payment amount, or by creating a new PaymentIntent with adjusted amounts.
Other line item updates, such as adding new line items, aren’t supported for this integration.
By default, an item’s minimum adjustable quantity is 0 and the maximum adjustable quantity is 99.
Checkout prevents the customer from removing an item if it’s the only item remaining.
After the payment completes, you can make a request for the finalized

findings: The November 7 root capture contains only a short purpose sentence and links to Full page (?ui=full-page) and Embedded form (?ui=checkout-form) variants; neither body is present (new raw lines 5-14). It cannot establish their setup, API, allowed quantities, client calls, or payment state behavior.

The April 21 full capture documents Checkout Session line-item adjustable_quantity configured on the server at Session creation with mode payment and ui_mode elements in its example (old raw lines 8-18, 23-47). The client-side updateLineItemQuantity example uses a line-item ID and new quantity, with HTML/JS and React forms (old raw lines 51-110). These are April, not November verified, integration details.

Old raw separately says Payment Intents API users must track line-item updates and adjust amount or create a new PaymentIntent (old raw lines 10-12). That is distinct from Checkout Session client updateLineItemQuantity; the current summary preserves the distinction in source lines 59-62.

The April guide bounds quantity adjustment: default minimum 0 and maximum 99, configurable maximum up to 999999, last remaining item cannot be removed, and other line-item changes such as adding items are outside this integration (old raw lines 14-18, 47-49). Current source lines 22-33 and 59-62 accurately retain these as historical claims, but its frontmatter and Raw Sources cite only the April raw (source lines 4-8, 70-72). Add the November navigational raw separately without renewing old behavior.

The current source summary calls this client-side quantity adjustment in Checkout Sessions without stating that the captured implementation sample is the Elements/custom Checkout route (source lines 11-13, 17-30, 35-45; old raw lines 23-44, 51-110). The new Full page/Embedded form labels do not prove those variants have the same client API. Qualify the historical UI scope in source and reciprocal Checkout concept line 146, which currently presents the client API without a route/date.

The old guide describes final-line-item retrieval after payment completes and shows checkout.session.completed handling with listLineItems limit 100; removed items are absent and internal IDs can be kept in metadata for reconciliation (old raw lines 113-115, 134-176). The fulfillOrder function is a throwing TODO (old raw lines 134-139), so source lines 47-57 should remain a dated pattern, not fulfillment-success proof.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/adjustable-quantity, new raw lines 5-14 establish only the purpose of customer quantity adjustment and navigation to Full page and Embedded form variants. No variant body is captured, so this does not establish a current API, prerequisites, or state boundary. The mapped source-stripe-checkout-adjustable-quantities.md summarizes this older path and post-payment finalized-line-item retrieval, but should date its UI scope rather than imply the new variants were examined.
